drivingQuestion: Until what hour does rainfall release the community from completing the fast?
outcomeNote: baraita records a tannaitic dispute; continued by R' Yosei in the next unit

segments.he: הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין וְיָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים קוֹדֶם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין וְיָרְדוּ לָהֶם גְּשָׁמִים, קוֹדֶם הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה — לֹא יַשְׁלִימוּ. לְאַחַר הָנֵץ הַחַמָּה — יַשְׁלִימוּ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: קוֹדֶם חֲצוֹת — לֹא יַשְׁלִימוּ. לְאַחַר חֲצוֹת — יַשְׁלִימוּ.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If «they were fasting» for rain «and rain fell for them before sunrise,» they need not complete their fast until the evening. «The Sages taught:» If «they were fasting» for rain «and rain fell for them before sunrise,» they need «not complete» their fast, as the obligation to fast does not come into effect until sunrise. However, if rain fell «after sunrise, they» must «complete» their fast. This is «the statement of Rabbi Meir. Rabbi Yehuda says:» If rain fell «before midday,» they need «not complete» their fast; however, if it rains «after midday, they» must «complete» their fast.
